text: Whether built screen by screen or through rapid implementation spreadsheets, an enterprise structure should never go live untested. This lesson covers the review a careful consultant runs before calling it done.

A checklist spanning the whole course: legal entities, the ledger's chart of accounts and calendar, balancing segment values, business unit functions, reference data sets, calendar periods, enabled currencies, segment labels, hierarchy rollups, and cross-validation rules.

A cross-validation rule that's never actually rejected anything hasn't been tested, just assumed to work. A real test deliberately attempts a known-bad combination and confirms it's rejected, and a known-good one and confirms it's accepted.

Before trusting a hierarchy-based report, pull a known parent's total and manually verify it matches the sum of its expected children. A misattached child produces a quietly wrong number, not an obviously broken one.
Every item on this checklist is dramatically cheaper to fix before live transactions post than after. Next up, lesson twenty-nine: common enterprise structure mistakes.
